title: First moment of the free-variable count under a Bernoulli restriction
statement:
Fix $n$ and a real number $p$, and let $\rho$ range over all restrictions on the $n$ variables, each weighted by its Bernoulli weight $w_p(\rho)$. Writing $J(\rho)$ for the set of free variables of $\rho$, then for every set $U$ of variables,
\[
  \sum_{\rho} w_p(\rho)\,\abs{U \cap J(\rho)} \;=\; p\,\abs{U}.
\]
Equivalently, when $0 \le p \le 1$ so that $w_p$ is a probability distribution, the expected number of free variables landing in $U$ is $p\,\abs{U}$.
hypotheses_covered: p is an arbitrary real number
U is a set of variables (subset of the index set)
replaced:
Under a Bernoulli($p$)-random restriction with free set $J$, for every set $U$,
\[
  \E\bigl[\abs{U \cap J}\bigr] \;=\; p \cdot \abs{U} .
\]
